summary.text: Acceleration measures how rapidly and in what direction an object changes its velocity.
Applying a net force to an object produces acceleration aligned with that force, proportional to the force's magnitude and inversely proportional to mass.
Acceleration includes both changes in speed and changes in direction, such as moving along a circular path at constant speed.

facts.label: Relativistic limit
facts.value: Relativistic effects grow as speeds near light speed

facts.label: Uniform acceleration example
facts.value: An object in free fall in a uniform gravitational field

items.prompt: If a car travels along a straight road while steadily picking up speed, what form of acceleration is taking place?

options.label: Linear or tangential acceleration
Radial acceleration
Deceleration or retardation
Centripetal acceleration

items.explain: When an object speeds up along a straight line without changing direction, the acceleration occurs in the direction of its motion, which is called linear or tangential acceleration.

items.prompt: A satellite orbits Earth in a circle at a steady speed. Why is it still considered to be accelerating?

options.label: Its mass decreases while orbiting.
Its direction of travel is constantly changing.
Its speed increases during each orbit.
It experiences a retro-rocket force.

items.explain: Acceleration includes changes in direction as well as speed; turning along a circular path causes centripetal acceleration even if speed stays constant.

items.prompt: How does doubling the total force on an object change its acceleration if the mass stays the same?

options.label: The acceleration is reduced by half.
The acceleration remains completely unchanged.
The acceleration doubles in magnitude.
The acceleration quadruples in magnitude.

items.explain: According to Newton's second law, net acceleration is directly proportional to the magnitude of the net force acting on the mass.

items.prompt: A stone falls near Earth's surface with no air resistance. What alone sets how fast its velocity changes?

options.label: The size and weight of the stone
The height it was released from
How hard it was pushed at the start
The strength of the gravitational field

items.explain: With no resistance to motion, a falling body's acceleration depends only on the gravitational field strength g.

items.prompt: Why is average acceleration considered the most fundamental way to measure acceleration?

options.label: It can be measured directly without appealing to empirical laws.
It is the only measurement that has a direction vector.
It eliminates the need to record elapsed time.
It remains constant regardless of applied net force.

items.explain: Average acceleration requires only the change in velocity and change in time, making it the only true acceleration measurable without relying on empirical physics laws.

items.prompt: What happens to the acceleration vector when a driver steps on the brakes to slow down a moving car?

options.label: The acceleration turns perpendicular to the path.
The acceleration acts opposite to the direction of velocity.
The acceleration vector drops immediately to zero.
The acceleration converts entirely into radial acceleration.

items.explain: Slowing down, often called deceleration, is acceleration directed opposite to the object's velocity vector.
